posts.title: Facts About the Arctic in November 2026
posts.description: At the beginning of November JAXA/ViSHOP extent is in a “statistical tie” with 2012 for 6th lowest for the date in the satellite era: In the continuing absence of the Alfred Wegener Institute’s Arctic sea ice concentration map, here once again is the AMSR3 based map from the University of Bremen: Read more on Facts About the Arctic in November 2026…

posts.title: Facts About the Arctic in October 2026
posts.description: The Arctic sea ice refreeze has started with a bang, and JAXA/ViSHOP extent is currently 17th lowest for the date in the satellite era: A large area of the Beaufort Sea melted late and has now refrozen swiftly: Read more on Facts About the Arctic in October 2026…

posts.title: Facts About the Arctic in September 2026
posts.description: With the 2026 minimum extent rapidly approaching, JAXA/ViSHOP extent is currently 12th lowest for the date in the satellite era: Despite the falling air temperatures, the AWI concentration map is still showing plenty of open water near the North Pole: Read more on Facts About the Arctic in September 2026…
